notes: Half day: US stocks close 13:00 ET (bonds early too). Scores still 2 of 12 (17%, all 50-65), below the ~50% no-skill baseline, so I keep confidence near 50 and make ZERO calls: the index gap is 1.5-2.4% (coach's rule: no intraday index call on a 2%+ gap) and no single-stock catalyst I could size. Wed Nov 25 lesson: I leaned QQQ down 52 / SPY up 51 on a gap down; both reversed up hard from 09:30 (our bars: SPY open 703.18, low 695.45, close 717.80, +2.08% open-to-close; QQQ 617.10 -> 634.31, +2.79%; TQQQ +8.96%). SPY up was right, QQQ down was wrong; the chip-unwind 'second leg' did not come, the gap was bought. Setup today (TipRanks 08:28 ET): Nasdaq-100 futures +2.35%, S&P +1.67%, Dow +1.44%; Upstox: S&P +1.53%, NDX +2%. Driver: dip-buying in AI/chips (NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, DELL named) after a heavy November selloff; Asia closed strong (KOSPI +4.3%, Shanghai +3.7%, Nikkei and Hang Seng +2.1%). TipRanks notes AI names 'have given back some of their early gains'. Oil: WTI ~$84.8 (+1.3%) on Hormuz shipping and Saudi-site attacks; Brent ~$96. No Fed/export/tariff headline over the holiday found (did not search deeply). Single names seen but not called: VRTX down (FDA extended povetacicept review up to 3 months; a delay, not a rejection; size unknown, delays often half-fade), MO down (considering buying part of Imperial Brands), SPCX up (Musk share-donation headline; not a catalyst I trust), RKLB/ASTS up (headline only). No Skylit credits used. Expected opens from Wed close: SPY ~728-730, QQQ ~647-650 (Wed closes 717.80 / 634.31; Tuesday's highs in our bars are not checked).

market_read.tone: Risk-on gap up into a thin Black Friday half day: AI/chip rebound continuation after Wednesday's full gap-down reversal; oil firm on Gulf attacks.

market_read.comment: Bias is open-to-close (09:30-13:00) from the gap open, not vs. Wednesday's close. Lean: slight fade, because gap-ups faded on Nov 12, 17 and 18, today's gap stacks on top of Wednesday's +2% / +2.8% intraday reversal (SPY open is ~3.7% above Wednesday's low in under 1.5 sessions), TipRanks already reports AI names giving back early gains, and holiday volume is thin. Against it: pre-holiday and Black Friday sessions lean firm, and Wednesday showed dip buyers are active; this is close to a coin flip. QQQ gets the bigger lean because its gap is larger and chip-led. Tripwire: at 10:15, if SPY and QQQ are above their 09:30-10:00 highs, drop both down leans (a drift-up half day); if QQQ is below its 09:30-10:00 low, the fade lean holds. Any index target should be small (0.4-0.6%) given the short session.
